_comment: CHURN CARD — D5 v5b: the CORRECTED carried-only guard.
(network.carry_invariant_innov_carried_only); what changed is the CODE behind it.  The
first implementation keyed the skip on the driver's chord_carried mask alone.  That mask
is TOPOLOGICAL — cycle in A_old, no slip — and says nothing about whether the carried
prior holds information: a chord carried from a predecessor that was itself diffuse
inherits a diffuse PROJECTED prior and passes it.  Measured on runs/churn_v5: after
skipping 13 643 rows, 7 082 of the 8 807 surviving flags (80.4%) were STILL at
sqrt(Cov(v)) = 1000 m, i.e. still untestable.  The guard now also skips a chord whose
Cov(v)_ii is at or above half of fresh_prior_var, which is the informational test the
GRADE against runs/churn_v5 (the defective arm, deliberately kept on disk) and
runs/churn_base2 (same-build baseline).  The expectation from v3 and v4 is that the
graded quantities do NOT move — this arm exists to close the question at the source
rather than leave it resting on a guard that only caught two thirds of its target.
